utterances.speaker: MATO TADIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: That is something that has to be resolved at a professional level.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: So then would you agree with me when I say that perhaps all of these rules were established in relation to the political project of setting up a constitution for this community and that perhaps one could not give to the military officials powers that would be significant in respect of the most serious crimes, given the very nature of the war that was being waged? Would that be an interpretation?

utterances.speaker: MATO TADIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I can give you the following answer: All the time attempts were made to build a civilian structure of authority in the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna. If too great an authority were to be given to the commander, then the civilian structure of government would be brought into question. What the political background was, that is something I really cannot answer because I never held any office within politics and the party, and I never held any posts related to that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Very well. That's as far as we'll go. Mr. Tadic, thank you. I hope that you will be able to get home, as you need to be. We have completed our work here. I would like to thank you. Once again, we are very grateful for you having come to The Hague and for having stayed longer than you had originally intended to. Mr. Dubuisson, will you have the witness taken out of the courtroom, please?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: I would like to know what I should do with 568 and 569, the Prosecution Exhibits.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: I was going to move that those two exhibits be introduced into evidence. One is a map and one is the decree appointing Mr. Tadic to his position.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Any objections?

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: All right. No objections.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Mr. President, Your Honours, I am pleased if I managed to help you at least a very little bit. I wish you every success in your work, in your very, very difficult and responsible work, but above all, your very honourable work.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you very much, Mr. Tadic. (The witness withdrew)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: We still have some time. Is Professor Jankovic available? Judge Shahabuddeen, shall we hear the Professor now? Mr. Hayman, he's here?

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: He is, and then we do have a witness who will be available at 2.30 after we're done with the Professor. We have one more witness this afternoon. I don't know if that witness will take the whole afternoon, but that witness is not here yet, the next witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: All right. Then we'll finish the morning with Professor Jankovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Mr. President?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Mr. Cayley?

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: It was simply actually a point of procedure. I wanted to have it clear in my own mind as to the procedure that is being adopted now with the Professor. My understanding is that he will make a presentation to the Court. You and your brother judge, Judge Shahabuddeen, will be asking him questions, and then Mr. Nobilo and I, although we're not allowed to ask questions of the witness at this stage, may make some representations to the Court. Is my understanding correct?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Yes. On the advice of my eminent colleague, we have somewhat changed the legal framework. We decided that rather than calling him as an expert amicus curiae, we will simply use Rule 98, that is, he becomes a witness again. In agreement with my colleague, you can ask him questions but assuming that the questions are brief. We don't want to start the Professor talking once again about everything he has already said. He's going to present -- maybe that is going to change. The Judges will ask him directly to give us a critical presentation, of course, in a broad sense, his presentation, I mean, on the diagrams that had been attached to Witness W; is that correct, Mr. Dubuisson?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: And then you can ask whatever questions you like, as can Defence counsel. Since this is a Defence witness, we'll start with Mr. Nobilo, and then it will be your turn, and, if necessary, the Judges will ask some questions, but the idea is that we should be able to finish, more or less, within 30 minutes. We're not going to start the entire testimony of the Professor from the beginning. You know, he's a very knowledgeable man in the field of explosives. We want to count the amount of time that's going to be used. All right. We can have the witness brought in. (The witness entered court)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you, Judge Shahabuddeen.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Professor Jankovic, you have been recalled pursuant to Rule 98. I'm going to ask you to take the oath again, please. Would you please rise? There is a statement which will be given to you. You've found it yourself.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Professor. Thank you for having been willing to remain here, remain available to the Tribunal. You're going to make a presentation that you were asked to do in respect of the diagram, and this falls within your area of competence, and then the Defence will ask you the questions it wishes to, the Prosecution will follow, and then perhaps the Judges, and then it will be finished. We hope that we can finish before 1.00. About how much time do you need in order to make your presentation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Five to ten minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Well, that's just fine. Take your time and make your presentation. Shall we put the document on the ELMO? All right. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN JANKOVIC (Recalled)
utterances.text: All right. This is the document I'm talking about. First of all, as you see, the scales have not been respected. Therefore, you've got 1.800 metres, and here you have 7.500 metres. You can see that, on this scale, the 1.800 is larger than the 7.500. Then you see that here, there is a height. I looked on the map. This figure is correct, that is, the top of a mountain. It is exactly in the eastern direction of Zenica. Therefore, that should be the trajectory vertically in the east/west direction. Here's the map. This is the mountain top which is in this direction (indicating); however, the other mountain top is this one (indicating) which is 600 metres. This is the Brankovac radius. It's not absolutely on this plane but a little north of that. So this is not absolutely a demonstration of the east/west direction. The trajectory which is shown here should be compared with the pictures that I showed you yesterday, I and C, I for OF 462 and C for the M76. For example, let's take the first one. I've also done the exact calculations in the east/west direction, and that's important because of the influence of the earth's rotation, and that has to be taken into account. Here you see the scales which were respected because this is computer produced. This is the mountain top where it was found, and you can see that the high is much higher, much higher than that point. The other one we were talking about, that is, the 600 metres is not at all important at this distance, which is noted in the original document, that is, at the distance of 1.800 metres. On 1.800 metres, you have the height of 1.519 metres. Therefore, that's three times higher, and if it's 800 metres, then the height for the M76 projectile would be 300 -- let me see, how much is that, 5 or 6 times higher. On this drawing, it should be 5 or 6 times higher. So what I would say, it's not even a good sketch. It gives a wrong impression. It gives the incorrect orientation, and it's more or less the same thing for the other projectile. I can repeat to you that the numbers are different. Here you have the top of the projectile, here's the mountain top, and here is the top of the projectory, the same thing over here at the start of the trajectory, and by making a comparison, you can see very clearly. On the copy of the document, I could say that, on this scale, you can't give exact results because the scale has not been respected, and everything I tried to do just didn't work. So, therefore, my conclusion would be to compare the document that you gave me with the two drawings because these are the ones where the scales have been respected, and I have referred back to these points in question. That's all I can tell you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Thank you. I would like to thank you for having spent another 24 hours in The Hague in order to do all these calculations.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN JANKOVIC (Recalled)
utterances.text: It was an honour for me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: I thank you so much. Would the parties like to make any comments? Mr. Nobilo, have you any comments you would like to make or Mr. Hayman?

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: As we have a new type of procedure, I'm not quite sure whether we should give precedence to the Prosecutor. They usually ask questions first. Only when we call our witnesses -- we did not call this witness, the Court called the witness, and I think that the initial impact is on the side of the Prosecution which would be more in keeping with procedure. So they can start their questioning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Mr. Nobilo, you are too clever a lawyer for these Judges who are very skillful themselves, but we can see what is underneath your question. Let's be serious for a moment here. We asked the witness, who is your witness, to come to make a scientific criticism of a Prosecution exhibit. If you want to make a comment, I suppose you do have some comments you would like to make, you can do so, and if you have to go back to what you want to say, then you can make further comments, but perhaps you don't have anything else you want to say.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: We have no comments to make, and as this is not a state of war, I think that procedure is important in every detail. As I say, we have no comments, no criticisms, but do we have the right to a redirect?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, have you the right to redirect. The Judges will take into account what you have pointed out to us, but I remind you that we, ever since the beginning of this trial, have wanted to be sure that the Rules are properly respected, and we have been vigilant in so doing. Mr. Cayley?

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. As is the case, my learned friend has very skillfully placed himself in an advantageous position, but I bow to your decision on this. I have very few questions for the witness. Cross-examined by Mr. Cayley:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Professor, you would agree with me that this diagram is not at all to scale, is it?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN JANKOVIC (Recalled)
utterances.text: That's what I said.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In fact, I think you would also agree with me that, in fact, this document is simply illustrative of the direction of a shell from a westerly position to an easterly position. That is all this diagram actually shows.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN JANKOVIC (Recalled)
utterances.text: No, that's not what it shows. It only shows that the projectile goes above Vranjaca Mountain, but we have to take into account the fact that it goes through Puticevo, Branke. In that case, you would be right, from Branke toward Vranjaca, that is, from west to east.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I think, as you pointed out to the Judges, the actual height of the trajectory is much higher than the two points indicated here at 820 metres and 600 metres, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN JANKOVIC (Recalled)
utterances.text: Yes, I showed that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So, in fact, all this diagram really demonstrates is that these were the two highest points over which the shell had to travel. It doesn't represent the actual trajectory of the shell, does it?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN JANKOVIC (Recalled)
utterances.text: Yes, but the scales have not been respected -- well, because the height of the mountain was 800 and then you have the top being 400, and one point is almost near the other.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So, as you've already said --

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN JANKOVIC (Recalled)
utterances.text: 4.000. Excuse me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As you've already stated, this is illustrative, this document is not to scale, is it?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN JANKOVIC (Recalled)
utterances.text: Yes, but if you permit me, I could say that it's not a good illustration.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, the line drawn from the weapon to the point of impact is not the trajectory line of the shell, is it?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN JANKOVIC (Recalled)
utterances.text: This diagram is not that, no. That's not this diagram.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In fact, the line of trajectory at its highest point would have been 5.000 metres, wouldn't it, or thereabouts?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN JANKOVIC (Recalled)
utterances.text: Would you repeat that question, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The actual height of the trajectory of the shell, at its highest point, would have been 5.180 metres, wouldn't it?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN JANKOVIC (Recalled)
utterances.text: As regards the projectile, the M76, the height is 3.788. That's for the OF4 D2. It's 4.506 metres.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What is the height of the trajectory with a standard OF 462?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN JANKOVIC (Recalled)
utterances.text: I just said, 4.506 metres.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that with a full charge or an additional charge?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN JANKOVIC (Recalled)
utterances.text: As you can see on the diagram, I gave you these figures for the initial velocity of 735 metres. So that's the maximum.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So all the line on this diagram represents, Professor, is simply the highest points over which a shell would have had to have travelled in order to reach Zenica, not its actual trajectory?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN JANKOVIC (Recalled)
utterances.text: Let's be careful about what we say. For the OF 462 -- actually 470. Excuse me. I've lost the picture here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: This is one time we shouldn't have lost the image. This is that moment. We are not going to have the witness come back yet again.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Apparently, there is a slight technical problem and it will be fixed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Do you have another question you want to ask?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN JANKOVIC (Recalled)
utterances.text: I can make a comment without the image. What I showed you just now, and we'll see it on the picture when it comes up, is the real image which the projectile would have had with the largest charge possible. That's my drawing, that is the drawing "I," and the height is 4.506 metres. This is not the greatest height that the projectile could have. They were talking about a howitzer, and a howitzer can be fired with very high angles, even 65 degrees, and then I can look in the tables, but it could have an order of magnitude of 6.000 and, therefore, the distance is much shorter.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Professor, I think we both agree that the actual trajectory of the weapon was much higher than 600 or 820 metres. The point that I am making to you is that the line on the exhibit that you've been given, Exhibit 230, can only represent the highest physical points on the ground over which the shell would have had to have travelled in order to reach its target. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Are you talking now about the exhibit which is in dispute? Yes. All right.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN JANKOVIC (Recalled)
utterances.text: I'm sorry, what do I have to answer?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: I think we are going to put the diagram of the exhibit which has been criticised back on the ELMO. Then you can ask the question again, Mr. Cayley, so that the witness can understand it properly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you agree with me, Professor, that all this diagram shows are the highest physical points on the ground over which the shell would have to travel in order to reach the target indicated on the right-hand side of the diagram? It doesn't show the trajectory, the actual trajectory of the shell, does it?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN JANKOVIC (Recalled)
utterances.text: Yes. I agree with that.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: I have no further questions, Mr. President. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Mr. Nobilo, have the Prosecutor's questions inspired you?

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: As usual. Re-examined by Mr. Nobilo:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Professor, take a look at the diagram that you have received. A gun has been drawn in here. From the fact that the line moves from the gun up to the region of the town of Zenica and the department store of Bosna, what did Witness W wish to show by that line? What did he want to show, not what he got? What did he want to show, if he had a gun on one side and the position where the shell fell on the other, and all this connected by a line?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN JANKOVIC (Recalled)
utterances.text: I understood that to be the trajectory. That's how I viewed it and I compared it with my trajectories.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is the full term used, ballistic trajectory for a line of this kind? Is that the term applied?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN JANKOVIC (Recalled)
utterances.text: This is a term which is used, but just what it means from a technical point of view is something else. I don't think I am going to get into that now. I don't want to go into those details.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. The term "ballistic trajectory" is sufficient for us. Now I come to my last question, Professor. What do you think about the level of professionalism for a man who draws a trajectory, a ballistic trajectory of this kind for an International Tribunal, that is to say the shell that represents a war crime? What do you think about his professionalism, the professional expertise of that witness?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN JANKOVIC (Recalled)
utterances.text: Well, I think that's somebody who really could not give an expert opinion. Absolutely not.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. That is all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: One little question, Professor. Would it have been possible for you to draw that sketch to scale so that we could see the representation of the actual trajectory of the projectile?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN JANKOVIC (Recalled)
utterances.text: Yes, and that's exactly what I did on diagrams "I" and "C." This is absolutely to scale, to real scale, although I did add here the top of the mountain, but tried to respect the scale. So you see here, this is the top of the mountain, and you can see how far above that mountain the trajectory is. This is a real scale. And the same thing here, that is the two diagrams. The diagrams came right out of the computer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: But I am talking about this sketch which you presented this morning. Would it have been possible for you to draw that one to scale?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN JANKOVIC (Recalled)
utterances.text: Excuse me. Could you make your question a bit clearer to me. I don't think I understand what you are saying. I prepared the diagrams using a scale which is noted here. That is, one kilometre is about one centimetre. The real scale would be impossible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: I see. It would have been impossible. That's your answer. I understand. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: I'd like, perhaps, one clarification. The angle of elevation at the initial point of the fire is, of course, very important. It's the firing person who is going to decide what it will be in respect of the target.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN JANKOVIC (Recalled)
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: I don't have the controversial drawing in front of me. What was the angle of fire that was used? It's not marked, but that was perhaps a supplement to what Judge Shahabuddeen asked. I can't really read it properly here. When you chose this firing angle, are these angles that you chose arbitrarily or was that in respect of the 16 kilometres separating Zenica?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN JANKOVIC (Recalled)
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: You reconstituted the process going backwards?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN JANKOVIC (Recalled)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: All right. If there are no further comments. Mr. Dubuisson. Mr. Cayley.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: I just think that the diagrams that the Professor has produced, and I'm sure Mr. Hayman will agree with me here, that they actually be made exhibits for the Court, because the good Professor has made certain marks on Exhibit 230, which will be of help both to the Prosecutor and to the Defence and to the Judges.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Yes. I'm sure that the Defence would not refute the fact that these two exhibits -- I suppose this is Defence material now. What I mean is the Defence would not object this time to have these two corrected drawings be numbered as Defence exhibits, and not as Prosecution exhibits. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Yes, of course, we do agree.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: All right. That way I think I am respecting the procedure, Mr. Nobilo. I think that with a smile on our faces and with a great deal of gratitude we must say -- express our gratitude to Mr. Jankovic, who agreed to remain available to international justice that we represent here, that is to stay another 24 hours in The Hague. I see the registrar is turning to me. Perhaps I made a mistake.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: I just want to say for the transcript that the drawing is 230, Prosecutor Exhibit, and the other exhibits, that is those of which the witness based himself, is D526. I also draw your attention --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: There are two exhibits.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Let me draw your attention to the fact that since this witness, who is a witness who is appearing now pursuant to Rule 98, perhaps it would be proper to set up a Trial Chamber's exhibit list so that the two exhibits that were noted by the witness, including the top of the mountains, should be noted as C1.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Why C?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: For Trial Chamber.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Well, if that's how it has to be, I suppose that's all right. Do you agree with that, Mr. Nobilo? All right. I'll take away the number. Do you agree, Mr. Hayman? Very well. Thank you very much, Professor Jankovic. We are going to suspend the hearing for lunch break and we will resume -- just a moment, please. We will resume at 2.45 with your witness, Mr. Hayman and Mr. Nobilo. The Court stands adjourned. --- Luncheon recess taken at 12.52 p.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: We will resume the hearing now. Have the accused brought in, please? (The accused entered court)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Mr. Nobilo?

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Mr. President, the next witness would like to be heard in closed session and be assigned a pseudonym. I can explain the reasons for this but, once again, in a closed session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: All right. First of all, we will move into a closed session for you to explain the reasons, unless there is an objection from the Prosecution. If you have any objections, then we don't have to do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: No objections, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: All right. Closed session. Have the witness brought in. He will be given a pseudonym and it will be what?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It will be Witness DV.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Let's first move into closed session. (Closed session)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: 5.10 p.m., to be reconvened on Friday, the 22nd day of January, 1999 at 10.00 a.m.
